subject: POC: Fintera trial environment decision & success criteria
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@fintera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: POC kickoff follow-up — environment options & quick success criteria

Hi Olivia —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff: 

Summary of ask: Fintera wants a 3-week POC to validate low-latency inference and key integration flows for your fraud-detection feature set, then decide between a production move to Dedicated or VPC.

What we need you to confirm:
- Primary success criteria (suggested below)
- Preferred trial topology: Hosted sandbox, Dedicated sandbox, or VPC trial
- Point of contact for networking/procurement (I think Raj Patel is the budget owner?)

Suggested success criteria (please edit):
- Functional: model responses integrated into existing pipeline for 3 representative flows
- Performance: 95th-percentile latency < 200 ms for single-request generation, sustained throughput 20 req/s for batch-run tests
- Cost: unit cost per 1k requests under $X (we can refine once we see workload)
- Stability: no more than 2 errors per 1,000 requests during stress window

Environment options (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest onboarding) — minimal network setup, fastest time-to-first-test; good for functional/integration checks but not ideal for compliance/rules requiring customer VPC.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity) — predictable performance, good for load tests and longer runs; data isolation via tenant boundary; faster than VPC to set up for most customers.
3) VPC trial (private deployment) — best for compliance & auditability; requires network team coordination, IP allowlists, and longer lead time.

Attachments: I've attached a short POC checklist to capture roles/timeline and a SOC2 summary that procurement might ask for.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria & kickoff date
- Week 1: integration + basic smoke tests (hosted sandbox recommended to move quickly)
- Week 2: load testing (Dedicated sandbox)
- Week 3: VPC validation (if you want final acceptance in a VPC)

Can you confirm which environment you prefer to start with (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and who on your side owns networking? I'll book a 30-min kickoff once we confirm.

Thanks —
Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Grant <olivia@fintera.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintera.com>, James Liu <james@fintera.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC kickoff follow-up — environment options & quick success criteria

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few notes from our side: 

1) Compliance: We will need the final validation to happen in our VPC, however we'd like to avoid full VPC setup for the first smoke tests. Ideally we can: start in a Hosted sandbox for initial integration, then do load testing on a Dedicated sandbox, and finally run a short VPC validation window. Does Redwood support that hybrid flow?

2) Procurement: Raj is correct — he owns budget approval. Our rough timeline is: procurement approval by the end of May, POC acceptance mid-June. We may need a one-page MSA addendum for the POC — can you send a template?

3) Network: James will coordinate with our network/security team. I'll introduce him to your SEs once we schedule kickoff. He's CC'd.

4) Success criteria: The latency numbers look good. For cost targets we don't have a firm $X yet — we need an estimate from you after you see our sample volume (I can share a 48-hour sample traffic export).

Please also attach your SOC2 report or a summary we can pass to procurement.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Product, Fintera

Subject: Re: POC kickoff follow-up — proposed evaluation plan & responsibilities

Hi Olivia / Connor —

Yes — hybrid flow is what we recommend for most regulated fintech customers. Below is a concise, actionable evaluation plan and a recommendation for the environment sequencing.

Recommendation (sequence):
- Phase A (Days 0–3): Hosted sandbox 
  - Purpose: quick integration + verification of API, auth, and basic response checks
  - Deliverables: sample calls working end-to-end, basic logging integrated
- Phase B (Days 4–11): Dedicated sandbox (2x GPUs equivalent) 
  - Purpose: stress/load testing + throughput/latency baselining under sustained load
  - Deliverables: load test report, 95th latency numbers, error-rate analysis
- Phase C (Days 12–18): Short VPC validation window (if you choose VPC) 
  - Purpose: compliance checks, audit sampling, network egress validation
  - Deliverables: final acceptance sign-off, audit artifacts

Suggested success criteria (refined):
- Integration: 3 production-like flows exercise end-to-end (match our checklist)
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 200ms at 20 req/s sustained for 5 minutes during load run
- Reliability: < 0.2% error rate during acceptance tests
- Security/Compliance: Connectivity validated to your VPC, audit logs available for a sample period

Ownership (high level):
- Redwood: provision hosted + dedicated sandboxes, run load tests, provide SOC2 summary and network diagram, create rollout/fallback policy for model variants
- Fintera: provide test dataset (anonymized), firewall rules and IP allowlist, procurement sign-off (Raj), internal acceptance sign-off (Olivia)

Network notes: For the VPC trial we'll need the following from James's team: two IP ranges to allow, an engineer to accept a short maintenance window for routing tests, and an SSH endpoint for diagnostics (read-only). I've attached a simple network diagram and the Redwood POC checklist for your internal IT team.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: VPC lead time delays — Mitigation: run Phase A/B in Hosted/Dedicated to preserve momentum
- Risk: dataset mismatch — Mitigation: run smoke tests with Redwood's synthetic data first then swap to your sample

Next actions I can do this week:
- Prep Dedicated sandbox and a load test plan (ETA 48 hours after kickoff)
- Share SOC2 summary (attached) and a short network checklist link

Attachments: [network-diagram.png], [Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf]

Thanks —
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
